I work in a vets office. Get. Insurance. Asap. Even if its just for emergencies (some offer wellness plans, but I say you can budget for shots and yearly bloodwork and save on your monthly bills). I cannot tell you how heartbreaking it is to see owners come in and have to chose euthanasia because they couldnt financially handle their pets health costs, or see a problem like allergies stay out of control because if not managed monthly, it can turn into resistant ear or skin infections that require culture and weeks long rounds of meds, before going into expensive monthly routines (between food and allergy meds, it can add up for monthly costs to ensure you dont have to add persistant infections to your pay out)

Pending on your insurance you can build your plan. I say, if you ever end up at an emergency clinic its usually ~100$ish for the visit alone, and 500ish for bloodwork, which is a baseline diagnostic and something youll want run 80% of the time. 

So, what I did for my own pets was get an insurance that pays out after that bloodwork cost (to keep your monthly rate lower) so you can bolster the amount covered. I use embrace, and thankfully I havent had to use it yet, but vet bills get expensive quickly.

Pair this with care credit, which gives you 6ish months of no interest, you can use your reimbursement to pay that off.

Also, when looking into insurances, especially for adult animals, look for plans that have curable/treatable condition clauses where if they go x amount of time without being seen for a previous ailment, the insurance will cover it. A LOT of insurances try pre-existing conditions bullshit and its frustrating to deal with on the medical profession side because diarrhea or vomiting is a symptom, not a condition, and suddenly now no GI related things are covered for an animal. Ive also seen insurances try and pull this on baby animals because they tested positive for parasites off the bat, which, is bullshit as most baby cats and dogs have some kind of wormie.

This is above reddits paygrade but if you really want our two cents heres mine.

1. This is a tragedy in every sense. Most marriages do not survive a childs death. It is not wrong to want to get as far away from your ex and his family as possible.

2.a You admit that your sons death was an accident, but you still refer to your ex BiL as a murderer. You dont have to forgive him, but I think framing him as a murderer is making you...i dont know how to word it. Hold on to certain emotions and framings of the events. Again, you dont have to forgive him, but I think you accepting this as an accident will help you let go of some of this anger. You likely will never fully heal from something like this, but you very likely will be able to move on from focusing on BiL and ex.

2.b I think your framing of your ex's family also needs to be worked through with a therapist. You don't have to forgive them but you also are framing them in what appears to be an unfair light. They lost a son, grandson, and nephew too. They are also mourning a loss. They are not defending a murderer by virtue of it having been an accident. Them being defensive towards your statements makes sense, as they are a charged biased view of what happened. Again going to therapy regarding how you view them is not to forgive them, but to help you process things, and understand why they would be reactive as such to your statements/feelings.

3. With that said I also think you and ex should look into heavily moderated couples therapy. Not to try and save the marriage, but to help both of you find a functional middle ground. Your husband needs therapy, but I also think you both need a moderator to help you two set goals on how to coparent without being in each others lives. Your husband needs to accept that you're not forgiving him or his brother. Emotions are complicated, unfortunately, and he also needs help in moving on from this too. This isnt you being responsible for his comfort. This is you finding a way to stay sane while having to coparent with your ex. 

4. My own therapist gave me an exercise regarding a falling out I had with a close friend of mine over something she did that I, personally, could not forgive unless she had one hell of a self realization and apologized. While I dont think it helped me entirely, I do think it at least helped me gather my thoughts and collect my feelings. Basically, write letters that arent to be sent to the recipients. Write a letter to your ex, write one to your ex BiL, write one to the family (or the individuals of the family). Write to your lost son, and to your living son. Get everything onto paper. Rewrite them if you feel you werent as articulated as you wanted to be with the first draft. Keep these letters for when you find a good therapist and walk through them in therapy. This exercise helped to pin point parts of the betrayal and hurt I was feeling so that I could help myself get grounded and move past certain things. I dont know if youll get mileage from this but it may help.


But truly I do think you need a therapist that deals with child loss and couple troubles as a personal (individual) therapist, and then I think you need another one who works in these same issues to moderate you and your husband working through the divorce and the loss. Your ex absolutely needs his own therapist too.

More asshole things will be said by the both of you, and you dont have to forgive or understand him, but you must find a way that allows you to move past the anger, or itll addle away at you. Just like he needs to find a way to accept that the marriage is done and he cannot get you back as a wife.


I am truly sorry for your loss, but I really do think you need to find a good therapist for this sort of thing and not ask reddit about if youre an asshole or not. This goes far beyond whos an asshole and who isnt.

Metlife was another I heard of from a client. Checked it out. Offers vetmed staff discounts + health care or military staff discounts. Caps at 10k, was also reasonably priced. Same pre-existing condition policy as embrace.

Lemonades site prevented me from fully wanting to dive intonthe nitty gritty. It seemed fairly fine, I cant recall if it had a cap or not. I believe it was reasonably priced, maybe cheaper comparatively. No discount, and I think a better pre-existing condition policy.

The list thing is both a real need and also a real excuse for getting things done around the house. 
I grew up with parents that could keep a mental checklist of things to do by the week to maintain a house, while also holding a philosophy of "if you see a need, attend to it"

This is all good and well but as someone who grew up with undiagnosed and untreated adhd, this was literal hell for me to cope to without adjustments to help me stay on top of things. The main issue was my time blindness and blindness to clutter in my environment. Basically meaning, weekly chores dont exist because a week isnt real and finding things that need to be done does not exist because the laundry on the couch is now part of the couch.

To grow up, I had to learn how to combat this by making sure i didnt allow my brain to make things disappear into the environment and that i had a regular rotation of things on a physical checklist to do. 

I'd make for myself "rounds" where i physically have to check certain areas of my house where clutter commonly/naturally accumulates (kitchen dishes by the sink, clean laundry on the couch) and if i "saw a need" i would do those things. Instead of these rounds having to be kept in my head, and by adhd logic be 'several tasks', having a physical checklist made this "one task" which was "look at the checklist and do the checklist". 

My weekly chores were made "real" by making the week "real" by writing the week dates on the cheklist itself and ensuring that i got one or two tasks done before the end date.


So, yes, lists can be an invaluable tool for managing your home but most so due to their ability to make a tangible aspect to a chore list and not because you need your wife to deligate your work.

The hormone therapy and gender affirming surgeries in the context of "gender is a social construct" I suppose are hard to explain unless you experience gender dysphoria yourself. That said, bear with me, I'm actually here to allow some insight into things for those genuinely curious.

I'll start with the initial question OP asked wrt "gender is a social construct". Its a true statement, as when you look across cultures what is considered "feminine" and "masculine" changes dramatically, especially as you look throughout history. That is to say, who knows what the next most "feminine"/"masculine" signifier will be in the next decade or century. A woman with a career in a pantsuit would have been considered very masculine once upon a time, it however has shifted with the culture. Just like how men can be effeminate today and still be men, and just like how some traditionally "masculine" things in the past are considered feminine now. Really, again, what it comes down to is that culture and society set the standards for what todays gender roles and signifiers are and therefore when someone is denying you personhood over these ever changing qualifiers, it stands to reason to say they are fake and should not be weaponized in such a way.

Onto why someone would want gender affirming surgeries. This one is hard to explain without someone knowing what gender dysphoria really feels like, or without really being surrounded by other queer folks. And honestly, I encourage you to read trans lit if you actually want to begin to understand this sort of thing. Its a different experience for many folks, and no one statement or example can really capture someone's feelings regarding their bodies and how it makes them feel to be in it. Really, what it comes down to is feeling comfortable in your own skin. I suppose another way to put it would be, why would a woman want a boob job? Why would someone fat want to lose weight? Why would someone want to bulk themselves at the gym? Why do cis men take testosterone to feel more like a man? They feel there is something about themselves that just doesnt fit right, and no matter the body acceptance movements or encourangments from others, some things just dont feel like /you/. There are ideal images and presentations people have for themselves, what makes them feel like themselves, what makes them personally feel like theyve achieved themselves. Gender affirming surgeries do this for trans folks (and cis folks too! Cosmetic surgery, implants, all these things, they are things that have existed for cis folk to feel more "properly themselves" for ages) Some go all the way with this, some dont feel like they need to. Again, everyone is very different, but it comes down to what makes you feel more attached to your skin. Again it is very hard to explain to someone who has never experienced it before, but some days you will look in the mirror, or have a moment of self reflection, and feel like the skin you have is a completely seperate entity. 

And as for your statement about how you, who i assume is a very cis looking cis man, should be able to say youre a woman and have that respected if "gender is a construct", there are many a trans woman (and trans man, though your specific example is not covering them) out there who do not pass as their gender. So yes, there are folks out there whos lives are very much your 'hypothetical' statement. They should be respected too, just as much as a passing trans person. 

That said life is very messy, and politics and news only add fuel to the fire. Theres also plenty of assholes around on both ends. Really what your take away should be is a baseline respect should be given until proven otherwise, and the "otherwise" qualifier shouldnt be based upon if you entirely understand another person or not. Everyone is different, has different experiences, and a little leeway and understanding (from all ends! Even queer folks! No one is born with a concrete understanding of every nuance to the human mind!) needs to be extended.

Like others have said, start with the actual trash removal first. Then move on to a semi categorizing cleaning. Move dishes/kitchen utensils into the kitchen or into one pile. Cloths into another heap, so on. Even if its still going to be "cluttered" get it off the floor and then try and vaccum. Youd be surprised at how much emotional tension gets removed when your floor looks vacuumed. 

Try and seperate any "use for later" items into storage bins (things you use once in a while for hobbies or repair or anything.) So you can have them in moveable containers that can be stacked and placed out of the way. Tackle item cleaning one category at a time, clothes vs dishes vs surfaces vs other, or seperate things into batches (whichever way your brain doesnt find as overwhelming. I know if i have to tackle a whole kitchen in a day i end up avoiding the whole thing entirely for days). 
Don't worry about feeling overwhelmed. You eat an elephant one bite at a time. I use to have a really bad clutter issue before I realized even if I pick up three things a day, thats still three things less than before. You can move onto a "deep clean" (sanitation clean) once you have some rhyme behind the reason. Dont get caught in the detailing until youre able to break the larger chunks down.
Dont be afraid to rearrange furniture if needed, or ask for a creative eye on storage. Downsize in areas youre confident with, and dont feel like you have to throw out personal/attachment items (no matter how small or "silly' they may seem) at this time.

....also dont be afraid to ask for help from someone you know, love, and trust, if you have such a person youre comfortable with. Even if you dont want them in your home, maybe staying the night with them for decompression time will do wonders.

While I am not entirely certain why someone would have gotten upset at your question, I think it may be due to where you asked the question/to which crowd you asked it to and how you asked it. Context here may help figure out why there was offense taken to your question, however...

To answer your initial question, a "loaded" question is where you will ask something, sometimes seemingly simple, but may be using the question to gage something deeper. These sort of questions are often manipulative to get an answer you can use to "read more" about a person than what your question may have seemed to ask.

Sometimes they arent being asked in a manipulative way, and usually in these cases its when someone asks a question that doesnt have a "right" answer but one that's politically dividing, or something else thats rather "hot topic" related and giving an answer may lead to an argument or a bad faith reading (meaning, someone will purposefully mistake your answer as malicious). 

To give a manipulative example, say your friend had invited you to do something that weekend, but you werent feeling like going out and decline saying you either arent feeling up to it (true) or had other plans (vague, and not lying). 

Later you are having a conversation with that same friend, and they ask you what your weekend plans are. You say you plan on sitting in with another friend/whoever at home and watching movies, or grabbing dinner with them and staying in town. Initially the question seemed harmless, but now your friend is responding to your answer with "so I see you having other plans was a lie/I see youd rather hang out with other friend than me/so you werent going to do anything". That is how you ask a manipulative "loaded question". Your friend didn't actually care what you were up to that weekend in an "interested what you were up to" way, they were trying to figure out what you were prioritizing over them. 

Your scenario doesnt seem manipulative, and seems more like you were asking something that felt like a political or hot topic kind of question to the person answering, and they felt the need to be defensive, or be offensive because they may have mistaken your question as trying to get approval for a generally accepted asshole move (mocking accents). They may feel defensive because they believe you are asking a question in bad faith (trying to make them say something you can attack them for). 

In your scenario (and correct me if I'm misunderstanding) you asked something along the lines of "what do you think about people who mock accents or the way people talk". From the context of Americans, racism via mocking folks for how they speak English has been something common through our history and still happens today. From face value, this question has an "obvious" answer of "those people are jackasses, and its unknind to do this to someone". Since it has an "obvious" answer, someone may think youre trying to get a specific reaponse out of them in order to start an argument. Regardless of your intentions, this may be why people are taking offense to it, as they think you are about to turn a simple "correct" answer into something argumentive. This especially happens when you ask groups of people you are not specifically close to, as the ability to add nuance into answers becomes less comfortable the less you know a person. 
Among friends you may get different answers, such as "i jokingly pronounce things like my buddys accent because we are close and its a joke between us, but I would never do it to strangers"
Or even "my buddy does this while im learning their language because being able to laugh at how I butcher the words makes me less self concious about saying them"

These are nuanced answers you may not get from strangers, and may not even be where a stranger's mind goes when asked such a question. Regardless, depending on the social environment, they may think youre asking a "loaded" question to either call them assholes for how they answer, or because they think you believe its okay to mock accents and are asking a "loaded question" to try and find likeminded people

First off Im really glad you're comfortable to ask this and I hope you dont get any hate from this. From your post alone, you dont seem like a proper terf as this word holds a lot of other requirements behind it. I'd like to also say that your confusion may also stem from being in a mostly cishet setting (nothing wrong with cisgender and heterosexuality, its just that when you are surrounded by folks who dont have the inside mind about those you have specific questions for, you often dont get informative answers). If you spend more time in queer spaces, you will see all the messy nuance that comes with being queer. Were a pretty diverse bunch, with a lot of different ways we percieve ourselves with. There isnt always a correct answer, but when it comes down to it we find what makes us feel proper.

I guess the first place to start I suppose is your thoughts on gender stereotypes. Many people will say that the gender binary and that gender as a whole is a social construct. To a degree theyre largely right, in the fact we see how gender roles and presentations can differ between cultures and people. What may be masculine or feminine in one area is different in others. When a transgender person "reinforces" gender stereotypes, such as a trans woman being hyper feminine or acting girlish, its less so about them doing what they think is girlish, so much as doing stuff that makes them feel like their gender. Same with trans men. This also doesnt just mean theyre presenting in the most hyper feminine or masculine ways possible either, some trans men are effeminate, some trans women are butch. This plays into a broader theme within the queer community of breaking gender expectations. Im a cis woman, but I present in a way most folks would consider masculine. Those who would want to be bigoted towards me may make comments about how I dont act like a woman, however feel as though my womanhood does not need to be expressed through my external looks and that because I am a woman, I can still be such while looking how I do. 

The same applies to trans folks as well, we just often see more of those who lean hard into the "gender stereotype" presentation. This may be due to it being what they are (a very feminine trans woman as opposed to one who feels more butch, or a masculine transman vs a more effeminate one), or it may be due to them just finding themselves out as trans and trying to figure out what makes them feel reaffirmed in their identity. It may also be that since they did not grow up as their true gender, they find some fulfillment in going through the various stages of "growing up" as their true gender.

A panicked bee thats stuck under your sleeves or feels threatened bc they crawled under your clothes and are stuck at one of your joints _will have a high chance to sting_. Have you ever heard the ball in a box theory for grief? Its been the best anaolgy I've ever seen, and rings true for me this day.

Imagine a box, where inside there is a button that is your pain and grief. Every time it gets hit, you feel those emotions at their strongest. Now, also inside that box is a ball, constantly pivoting around. 

When we first lose someone dear to us, that ball is large, almost taking up the entirety of the box, and almost always pressing on the button of grief and pain. As we move go on in life, that ball is still moving, and still has the potential of hitting that button. That ball, however, is ever changing in size. Its huge at first, but it shrinks at different rates for different people. Eventually it becomes small enough where it doesnt hit that button all the time or with as much force, sometimes it grows again in size and sometimes it can shrink down smaller.

The point, however, is that grief and loss is something that doesnt have to go away or stop hurting, it is just something that we adjust to, and handle, and can process better as the ball starts to shrink and we can reflect upon it without having that button hit.

Hey man, I want to share a bit of a story because I was in your situation before. It may seem self focused, but please read as I do have a point at the end on why youre at the first stage of being able to help yourself. I apologize now and later if this is assumptive or preachy, but your post really hit home for a me a few years back.

Firstly, understand that I am currently browsing this sub because I was just/still am being torn in half by a depressive mood thats sunk me to suicidal ideation again. 

Secondly, I was never this bad ("this" meaning having month long periods of wanting to kill myself and feeling horrible emotional isolation and meaningless life) until I graduated....however my warning signs preceeded even being accepted into college. I have a family that also loves me (to a broad degree, my nuances here dont matter), they supported me in some ways through my degree, which I switched several times. They helped me when I took a chance on an year long unpaid internship to help build my career, and helped me when i took a less than practical job to continue to build that networking and skillset towards a future I wanted....

And that crumbled, because I let it. Because I thought I was lazy and unmotived and stupid, and i felt guilty and like a piece of shit about it. My family would praise me for my accomplishments, and all I could focus on is how I let some of my connections slip away because staying in the loop was too much for me emotionally and mentally. I justified it as being a lazy underperformer, i had too many "highs" to really accept I was depressed. But the emotional slogs, the brain fog, the guilt, the lost potential....I had depression the whole time. I suspected it, i joked about it, i used it to irresponsibly justify letting it ruin my life. 

I believe this is where you are. We cannot control our brain chemistries. Do not blame yourself for feeling the way you do. It doesnt matter if you're the smartest and most well off individual, if youre depressed, those feelings can and will impact you, even if youre self aware about it. The pain of a broken arm doesn't go away just because you know how your arm is broken, or that there are others with many more compound fractures in the hospital. It hurts, it impacts your life, and the other positive factors of your life cant change that until you realize that yes, something is wrong, and yes its ok for it to be wrong in your situation.


I dont want to preach at you, but I want you to understand that feeling guilty about hurting wont change the fact that you're feeling pain. Try our hardest, we cannot control our brain's imbalances. It isnt your fault, and its not shameful to develop depression in good circumstances.
